newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INSIGHT - Australian All Industrials now back stuck in range.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INSIGHT - Australian All Industrials now back stuck in range.

text.p: ---------------Australian All Industrials Index-------------
---------------Analysis by Daniel Fock - Dec 11-------------
*Index still in ranges
*Indicators mixed
*Index bounces from short term channel support
The Australian All Industrials share index (Tuesday close 3,655.7) dropped over 100 points in one day only to recover some 80 points in two days.
The index is now back range-trading within the consolidation band of 3,645 to 3,715.
Traders are likely to be using the ranges and are likely to become agressive sellers if the double-bottom breaks at 3,573.
The bulls could be tiring.
Short term technicals are mixed. The averages are still bearish, but are bunched very close to the index and could turn quickly.
Leading indicators have experienced a slight up-tick.
This will have to continue to calm the sceptical bulls.
Retracement of the move down from 3,715 has almost fully completed, with the index stoping just four points short of 3,660.
Traders are likely to be cautious and see if the 3,645 level holds before buying.
In the medium term the index has broken initial support, but is back at the breakout.
Traders will still be concerned about the breakout of the bearish ascending wedge, but will be more interested to see if the double bottom at 3,573 holds in the medium term.
Medium term technicals are mixed.
Of particular interest is that the Stochastic has moved lower after 13 weeks, but with the sudden movement of the last three days, is turning back into the 80s again.
Traders will be monitoring this indicator in an effort to avoid the whipsaws.
If in fact last week's break down was not an abberation, traders are seen looking at the Fibonacci retracements of the much larger bull run since August, and target 3,507, 3,443 and 3,379.
Traders are unlikely to become agressive sellers unless 3,570 breaks.
In the longer term, the index is still bullish, but looks toppish, unless it can make further gains. The approaching end of year and Christmas, will only increase caution.
Longer term traders will be focusing on the next support level of 3,540.
Longer term technicals still remain bullish, but lower than last week.
Leading indicators have all slightly turned lower.
Traders are expected to generally wind back positions as the end of year approaches.

This is most likely to occur especially in the face of recent volitility. Notwithstanding the recent 100 point ranges, the index is ranging in 70 point bands, between 3,495 to 3,570, 3,570 to 3,645, and 3,645 to 3,715.
Technicals are suggesting some short term consolidation, but the medium and longer term are suggesting some correction lower in the new year.
Caution will be the key to trading between now and new year.
Traders will be eyeing the ranges and the retracement levels.
The index is still in the broad bull channels, but the bulls are running out of puff.
(Daniel Fock is a member of the Australian Technical Analysis Association. Views are his own, not those of Reuters.)
